observed_invariants.clock_reset: native work requires the firmware-enabled modem clock/reset domain; interrupts require the domain to have been enabled in the current reset generation but may assert or remain latched while firmware subsequently gates its functional clock; a reset-generation change retires in-flight activity and enable history
observed_invariants.wifi_dma: TX descriptor and payload pointers are nonzero four-byte-aligned internal-memory addresses; payload length is 1 through 4095 bytes; each firmware queue kick creates exactly one active hardware operation and exactly one status-nibble completion, with ACK, CTS or matching-TID block ACK selected from the transmitted MAC header and success, RF transmit error or response timeout selected by the observed outcome; retry policy remains in guest LMAC; native RX interface matches come from valid firmware-programmed address slots, with SoftAP using slot one; an active RX block-ACK slot must use the firmware-observed enable/mode encoding and its peer, TID, 12-bit origin and 64-bit bitmap remain register-backed
observed_invariants.bluetooth_le: native schedule records and security DMA must resolve through firmware-programmed internal-memory mappings before execution; connection-event sequence numbers, descriptor ownership and completion marks follow only genuine-firmware-observed transitions; the 100 kHz sleep timer accepts a future RTC compare followed by source-18 enable, permits firmware-observed armed cancellation, and permits pending clear only after expiry
observed_invariants.ieee802154: TX, RX, single-shot CCA, energy detection and ACK phases use the firmware command lifecycle and cannot overlap incompatibly
observed_invariants.coexistence: native Wi-Fi, Bluetooth LE and IEEE 802.15.4 RF submissions execute only under a matching grant returned for their firmware-selected protocol and priority; firmware reset generations and clock/power gating cancel active ownership and its exact in-flight transmission; denial is an ordinary non-submission outcome reported to Wi-Fi LMAC as the recovered transmit-error status, while cross-protocol ownership is a hard error

observed_invariants.bluetooth_le: scheduler slots, control structures, descriptors and payloads must use firmware-observed encodings and resolve through exchange-memory mappings; connection events are receive-first, fine/event metadata is bounded, and SN/NESN plus TX-ring ownership may transition only along the genuine-ROM sequence; the 1 MHz low-power sequencer accepts only duration-programmed, RF-sleep-acknowledged, wake-started and deferred wake-completion order
